title: Portable Trusted Linux
summary: Portable Trusted Linux is a portable security environment designed to boot independently of an installed operating system, authenticate its trusted components, collect TPM-backed boot evidence where available, verify an immutable Linux root, run with minimal persistence, produce independently verifiable attestation records, and preserve lessons and design history as the project evolves.

sections.title: Project objective
sections.content: Boot independently of a potentially compromised installed OS, authenticate the portable environment, collect hardware-backed evidence where available, protect the Linux root with dm-verity, keep normal state ephemeral, and allow a separate verifier to evaluate the resulting evidence. Every claim must distinguish what is proven, observed, assumed, unknown or not verifiable.

sections.title: Prototype 1 baseline
sections.content: Prototype 1 is now locked to Debian 13 trixie on amd64. Exact point release, package versions, build inputs, repository commit and artifact digests must be captured in each build manifest. The current Debian stable line is Debian 13/trixie; the project intentionally records exact build inputs rather than relying on the moving label stable.

sections.title: Runtime trust chain
sections.content: Authenticated release reference -> verified USB bytes -> UEFI/Secure Boot -> measured boot and TCG event log -> TPM PCR evidence -> signed UKI -> authenticated dm-verity root -> immutable Linux -> RAM-backed disposable state -> fresh nonce-bound TPM Quote -> independent verifier -> attestation report.

sections.title: Attestation report design
sections.content: The report no longer hashes a structure containing its own digest. Evidence is placed in a deterministic payload. The payload is canonicalised and SHA-256 hashed. An outer envelope contains the payload digest, signatures and future external-anchor receipts. Exact canonicalisation and cross-implementation test vectors remain a required implementation task.

sections.title: Mandatory lessons discipline
sections.content: Every meaningful engineering session, research result, test, failure, architecture change or implementation surprise must be written to docs/07-lessons-learned.md. Relevant technical documents and architecture decisions must also be updated. project_content.json is always the final repository write for the session.

sections.title: Negative testing
sections.content: Security features are not accepted solely because their happy path works. Prototype 1 now has a mandatory negative-test matrix covering altered images, unauthorised UKIs, dm-verity corruption, replayed/nonmatching nonces, modified TPM Quotes, missing event logs, TPM/Secure Boot absence, changed canonical payloads, broken history chains, network unavailability and RAM-persistence tests.

sections.title: External Evidence Anchoring
sections.content: Transparency-log and optional blockchain support remain part of the architecture, but Prototype 1 stops before public anchoring. The first engineering goal is to prove the local trust chain and independent verifier. External anchoring follows after canonical report generation and verification are stable.

sections.title: Current engineering work
sections.content: The repository now contains the first safe build scaffolding: shared shell helpers, host preflight, Debian Live preparation, package seed, attestation payload/envelope schemas and verifier design notes. Destructive USB-writing code is intentionally deferred until artifact verification and device-safety checks are implemented.

decisions.title: Reuse mature security primitives
decisions.text: Use Debian, UEFI Secure Boot, systemd UKIs, TPM 2.0 tooling and dm-verity rather than inventing a new kernel, bootloader or cryptographic stack.

decisions.title: Independent verifier is mandatory
decisions.text: The target machine cannot be the sole authority deciding its own evidence is acceptable.

decisions.title: External Evidence Anchoring added
decisions.text: Reports will support canonical hashing, signatures, previous-report linking and later independent publication of commitments.

decisions.title: Transparency log preferred; blockchain optional
decisions.text: Use a backend-neutral anchoring layer and do not publish complete private reports by default.

decisions.title: GitHub is the canonical development workspace
decisions.text: Project documents, build source, schemas and the living index are versioned in the private repository.

decisions.title: Lessons learned are mandatory
decisions.text: Every meaningful session/test/failure/change must update the Lessons Learned register and affected documents, with project_content.json updated last.

decisions.title: Prototype 1 baseline is Debian 13 trixie amd64
decisions.text: Exact point release and package versions are recorded per build; the moving stable alias is not sufficient provenance.

decisions.title: Attestation uses payload plus envelope
decisions.text: Canonical payload bytes are hashed; signatures and anchor receipts live outside that hash boundary to avoid a self-referential report hash.

decisions.title: Prototype 1 stops before public anchoring and polished UI
decisions.text: First prove the local verified boot/root/TPM/attestation chain with negative tests, then add transparency services and product UI.
